subject: math
title: Grade 2 Measuring Length: Centimetres, Metres and Rulers
seo_title: Grade 2 Measuring Length Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Direct linear measurement, introducing standard metric units
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on measuring length for the BC curriculum: see why we use standard units, choose centimetres or metres, read a ruler from 0 and from other points, compare lengths and solve word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Line up the object at 0 and count the spaces, not the marks.
key_sub: If it starts at 3 and ends at 10, it is 10 − 3 = 7 cm long. 100 cm = 1 m. Centimetres and metres are the same for everyone, so everyone gets the same answer.
body_html:
Measure with units that are all the same

Lay units end to end along the object. Start right at one end and stop at the other end. No gaps and no overlaps. Then count the units.

A paper clip is as long as 2 cubes. The same crayon is 6 cubes or 3 paper clips. A smaller unit gives a bigger number.

Why we use centimetres and metres

Two students measure the same mat with their hands. One gets 8 hands. The other gets 10 hands. Hands are not all the same size, so the numbers do not match. Centimetres (cm) and metres (m) are the same size for everyone, so everyone gets the same answer. Use cm for small things and m for long things. 100 cm = 1 m.

UnitAbout as long asGood for
1 cmthe width of your fingertipcrayons, pencils, leaves
1 m = 100 cmone big step, or a metre stickthe classroom, the hallway, the gym

Read a ruler from 0

Put one end of the object at the 0 mark. Look where the other end stops. Each space between two marks is 1 cm. Count the spaces, not the marks.

When the object does not start at 0

Count the spaces from where the object starts to where it ends. Or subtract: end − start.

Example

A crayon starts at 2 and ends at 6. How long is it?

Count from 2: 3, 4, 5, 6 is 4 spaces. 6 − 2 = 4.

Answer: 4 cm

Draw a line

Draw a line 5 cm long.

Start at 0. Draw to 5. The line covers 5 spaces.

Answer: Stop at the 5 mark

How much longer?

A ribbon is 45 cm long. A string is 28 cm long. How much longer is the ribbon?

Subtract: 45 − 28 = 17. Check: 28 + 17 = 45.

Answer: 17 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the marks (7 marks for 6 cm)Count the spaces between the marks
Starting at 1 or at the edge of the rulerLine up the end of the object with 0
Reading the end number when the object starts at 3Subtract the start: 10 − 3 = 7
Leaving gaps between cubesPush the units together so they touch
Thinking a bigger unit gives a bigger numberSmaller units give a bigger number
Saying “20 long” with no unitAlways say the unit: 20 cm or 20 m
Saying a pencil is 18 m longPicture a fingertip (1 cm) and a big step (1 m)

faq.q: What do Grade 2 students learn about measuring length in BC?
faq.a: In the Geometry and measurement area of the BC Grade 2 math curriculum, students measure length directly. They see why non-standard units like hands give different answers, then start using centimetres and metres.

faq.q: How many centimetres are in a metre?
faq.a: There are 100 centimetres in 1 metre. A fingertip is about 1 cm wide, and one big step is about 1 m.

faq.q: Why does my child get the wrong length on a ruler?
faq.a: The most common mistakes are counting the marks instead of the spaces, starting at 1, and reading the end number when the object does not start at 0. Ask your child to count the spaces, or to subtract: end − start.

faq.q: How can I practise measuring length at home?
faq.a: Measure toys and books with LEGO bricks or paper clips, then with a ruler in centimetres. Guess first, then check. Use big steps to measure a room in metres.

items.q: How many cubes long is the crayon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the crayon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them.

items.q: Count the cubes. How long is the key?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the key to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them.

items.q: How many paper clips long is the eraser?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the eraser to the other: 1, 2. It is 2 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them.

items.q: Count the cubes. How long is the pencil?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the pencil to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. It is 8 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them.

items.q: How many paper clips long is the straw?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the straw to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them.

items.q: Count only the cubes under the craft stick. How long is the craft stick?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the craft stick to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. It is 6 cubes long. There are 9 cubes in the row, but only 6 are under the craft stick. Do not count the extra ones.

items.q: Is this a good way to measure the crayon?
c: No, the clips are too small.
items.e: No, there are gaps between the paper clips. The gaps are not counted, so the number is too small. Push the paper clips together so they touch.

items.q: Is this a good way to measure the ribbon?
c: No, the clips are too small.
items.e: No, the paper clips overlap. Some lie on top of others, so you count too many. Lay them end to end.

items.q: The pencil is 8 cubes long. How many paper clips long is it?
items.e: Look at the bottom row. Count the paper clips: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 paper clips long. A paper clip is longer than a cube, so you need fewer of them.

items.q: A book is 10 cubes long. It is 5 paper clips long. Why are there more cubes?
items.e: A cube is shorter than a paper clip. It takes more cubes to cover the same book. Smaller unit, bigger number.

items.q: You measure a desk with cubes. Then you use paper clips. Which number is bigger?
items.e: A cube is shorter than a paper clip. You need more short units to cover the desk. So the cubes give the bigger number.

items.q: You measure the same table with each unit. Which unit gives the biggest number?
items.e: The smallest unit gives the biggest number. Linking cubes are the smallest here, so you need the most of them.

items.q: The paper clips do not fit exactly. How long is the pencil?
items.e: 3 paper clips are not long enough. 4 paper clips go past the end. So the pencil is between 3 and 4 paper clips long. Use smaller units, like centimetres, to be exact.

items.q: Emma and Kai measure the same mat with their hands. Emma gets 8 hands. Kai gets 10 hands. Why?
c: Their hands are not the same size.
items.e: Emma has bigger hands, so fewer hands fit. Units of different sizes give different numbers. That is why we use standard units, like centimetres and metres.

items.q: The teacher walks heel to toe across the rug. It takes 6 steps. Mateo does it too and takes 9 steps. Who is right?
items.e: The teacher has bigger feet, so fewer steps fit. Both are right, but the numbers do not match. A centimetre is the same size for everyone, so we use cm and m.

items.q: Why do we measure in centimetres and metres?
items.e: A centimetre is the same size on every ruler in BC and around the world. So everyone gets the same answer. Hands, feet and steps are different sizes for different people.

items.q: Noah says, “My book is 20 long.” What is missing?
items.e: 20 what? 20 cubes, 20 cm and 20 hands are not the same. Always say the unit, like 20 cm.

items.q: Arjun will tell his grandma in Kamloops how long his new scarf is. Which unit is best?
items.e: Grandma does not know how big his hands or steps are. Use a standard unit. A scarf is small, so use centimetres.

items.q: A paper clip is as long as 2 cubes. Owen’s box is 12 cubes long. How many paper clips long is it?
items.e: Each paper clip covers 2 cubes. Count by 2s to 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 jumps. The box is 6 paper clips long.

items.q: Simran’s towel is 6 big steps long. Her ribbon is 6 paper clips long. Which is longer?
items.e: Both numbers are 6, but the units are different. A big step is much longer than a paper clip. So the towel is longer. Always look at the unit.

items.q: Which is longer, 1 cm or 1 m?
items.e: 1 m is much longer. A metre is about one big step. A centimetre is about as wide as your fingertip.

items.q: What is about 1 cm wide?
items.e: The tip of your finger is about 1 cm wide. Use it to picture a centimetre.

items.q: What is about 1 m long?
items.e: One big step is about 1 m. A metre stick is 1 m long.

items.q: How many centimetres make 1 metre?
items.e: A metre stick has 100 small spaces. Each one is 1 cm. So 100 cm = 1 m.

items.q: About how long is a ladybug?
items.e: A ladybug is about as wide as your fingertip. That is about 1 cm.

items.q: About how long is a paper clip?
items.e: A paper clip is about 3 fingertips long, so it is about 3 cm. 3 m is about 3 big steps.

items.q: About how long is a crayon?
items.e: A crayon fits in your hand. That is about 9 cm. 9 m is about as long as a classroom.

items.q: About how long is a new pencil?
items.e: A new pencil is a bit longer than your hand. That is about 18 cm. 18 m is longer than a school bus.

items.q: About how wide is a classroom door?
items.e: A door is about as wide as one big step. That is about 1 m.

items.q: Which would you measure in metres?
items.e: Metres are for long things. The hallway is long. A crayon, a paper clip and an eraser are small, so use centimetres for them.

items.q: Which would you measure in centimetres?
items.e: Centimetres are for small things. A mitten is small. The field, the yard and the rink are long, so use metres for them.

items.q: Which tool is best to measure the classroom?
items.e: The classroom is long. A metre stick is 1 m long, so you need only a few. A short ruler, cubes or a paper clip would take a very long time.

items.q: About how tall is a door?
items.e: A door is taller than a grown-up. It is about 2 metre sticks tall: 2 m.

items.q: About how tall is a Grade 2 student?
items.e: A Grade 2 student is a bit taller than a metre stick. 1 m is 100 cm, so about 120 cm makes sense.

items.q: About how long is a grown-up orca?
items.e: A grown-up orca is about 7 big steps long. That is about 7 m. 7 cm is shorter than your finger.

items.q: About how long is a school bus?
items.e: A school bus is about 12 big steps long: 12 m. 1 m is only as wide as a door.

items.q: About how long is the school gym?
items.e: A gym is about 30 big steps long. That is about 30 m. 30 cm is about as long as a ruler.

items.q: A table is 2 m long. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: 1 m is 100 cm. 2 m is 100 + 100 = 200 cm. The number of centimetres is bigger because a centimetre is shorter.

items.q: Which is longer, 1 m or 90 cm?
items.e: 1 m is 100 cm. 100 cm is more than 90 cm, so 1 m is longer. Do not just look at the bigger number.

items.q: Leah’s rope is 1 m long. Harjot’s rope is 120 cm long. Whose rope is longer?
items.e: 1 m is 100 cm. 120 cm is more than 100 cm, so Harjot’s rope is longer.

sets.title: Read a ruler that starts at 0

items.q: You measure with a ruler. Where do you put one end of the object?
c: at the edge of the ruler
items.e: Put the end at 0. Some rulers have a little space before the 0, so do not use the edge. If you start at 1, the number at the end is 1 too big.

items.q: How long is the eraser?
items.e: The eraser starts at 0 and ends at 3. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cm long. There are 4 marks but only 3 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the key?
items.e: The key starts at 0 and ends at 4. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 cm long. There are 5 marks but only 4 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Measure the paper clip. How long is it?
items.e: The paper clip starts at 0 and ends at 3. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cm long. There are 4 marks but only 3 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 5. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cm long. There are 6 marks but only 5 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the leaf?
items.e: The leaf starts at 0 and ends at 6. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. It is 6 cm long. There are 7 marks but only 6 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Measure the caterpillar. How long is it?
items.e: The caterpillar starts at 0 and ends at 7. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. It is 7 cm long. There are 8 marks but only 7 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the worm?
items.e: The worm starts at 0 and ends at 8. Count the spaces: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. It is 8 cm long. There are 9 marks but only 8 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: What do you count to find a length on a ruler?
c: the last number on the ruler
items.e: Each space from one mark to the next is 1 cm. Count the spaces, not the marks. A 3 cm eraser covers 3 spaces but touches 4 marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 9. It is 9 cm long. There are 10 marks but only 9 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Measure the straw. How long is it?
items.e: The straw starts at 0 and ends at 10. It is 10 cm long. There are 11 marks but only 10 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the marker?
items.e: The marker starts at 0 and ends at 11. It is 11 cm long. There are 12 marks but only 11 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the craft stick?
items.e: The craft stick starts at 0 and ends at 12. It is 12 cm long. There are 13 marks but only 12 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Measure the pencil. How long is it?
items.e: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 13. It is 13 cm long. There are 14 marks but only 13 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the strip of paper?
items.e: The strip of paper starts at 0 and ends at 14. It is 14 cm long. There are 15 marks but only 14 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How many centimetres long is the ribbon?
items.e: The ribbon starts at 0 and ends at 15. It is 15 cm long. There are 16 marks but only 15 spaces. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Zara drew this red line. How long is it?
items.e: The line starts at 0 and ends at 7. It covers 7 spaces, so it is 7 cm long. There are 8 marks, but count the spaces.

items.q: Owen wants to draw a line 8 cm long. He drew this much. How many more centimetres must he draw?
items.e: The line ends at 5. Owen needs to get to 8. Count on from 5: 6, 7, 8. That is 3 spaces. 8 − 5 = 3, so he must draw 3 cm more.

items.q: Sofia draws a line 6 cm long. She starts at 0. Where should she stop?
items.e: Start at 0 and draw to 6. That covers 6 spaces, so the line is 6 cm long. If you stop at 7, the line is 7 cm long.

items.q: Ava measures a straw. It covers 12 spaces on the ruler and touches 13 marks. How long is the straw?
items.e: Each space is 1 cm. Count the spaces, not the marks: 12 spaces is 12 cm. There is always one more mark than spaces.

sets.title: When the object does not start at 0

items.q: How long is the eraser?
items.e: The eraser starts at 1, not at 0. Count on from 1: 2, 3, 4. That is 3 spaces. Or subtract: 4 − 1 = 3. So it is 3 cm long. 4 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The crayon does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The crayon starts at 2, not at 0. Count on from 2: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. That is 5 spaces. Or subtract: 7 − 2 = 5. So it is 5 cm long. 7 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: How long is the key?
items.e: The key starts at 3, not at 0. Count on from 3: 4, 5, 6. That is 3 spaces. Or subtract: 6 − 3 = 3. So it is 3 cm long. 6 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The leaf does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The leaf starts at 1, not at 0. Subtract: 8 − 1 = 7. So it is 7 cm long. 8 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The end of Ryan’s ruler broke off, so it starts at 4. He puts a paper clip at the 4. The paper clip ends at 7. How long is it?
items.e: Count from 4, not from 0: 5, 6, 7 is 3 spaces. 7 − 4 = 3, so the paper clip is 3 cm long.

items.q: How long is the caterpillar?
items.e: The caterpillar starts at 4, not at 0. Count on from 4: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 5 spaces. Or subtract: 9 − 4 = 5. So it is 5 cm long. 9 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: The paper clip does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The paper clip starts at 5, not at 0. Count on from 5: 6, 7, 8. That is 3 spaces. Or subtract: 8 − 5 = 3. So it is 3 cm long. 8 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: How long is the marker?
items.e: The marker starts at 2, not at 0. Subtract: 10 − 2 = 8. So it is 8 cm long. 10 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Ethan’s ruler starts at 3 because the end is broken. A marker starts at 3 and ends at 11. How long is the marker?
items.e: Subtract the start from the end: 11 − 3 = 8. The marker is 8 cm long.

items.q: The worm does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The worm starts at 6, not at 0. Subtract: 13 − 6 = 7. So it is 7 cm long. 13 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: How long is the straw?
items.e: The straw starts at 3, not at 0. Subtract: 12 − 3 = 9. So it is 9 cm long. 12 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Nadia puts the end of a crayon at 1, not at 0. The other end is at 9. She says the crayon is 9 cm. What did she do wrong?
items.e: The crayon starts at 1, so 9 is too big. Count from 1 to 9: 9 − 1 = 8. The crayon is 8 cm long.

items.q: The pencil does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The pencil starts at 1, not at 0. Subtract: 11 − 1 = 10. So it is 10 cm long. 11 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: A pencil starts at 3 and ends at 12 on a ruler. Lucas counts the marks from 3 to 12 and gets 10. How long is the pencil?
items.e: Count spaces, not marks. From 3 to 12 there are 10 marks but only 9 spaces. 12 − 3 = 9, so the pencil is 9 cm long.

items.q: How long is the craft stick?
items.e: The craft stick starts at 5, not at 0. Subtract: 14 − 5 = 9. So it is 9 cm long. 14 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Jasleen measures a key on a ruler. One end is at 5. The other end is at 9. How long is the key?
items.e: The key starts at 5, not at 0. Count the spaces from 5 to 9: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4. Or subtract: 9 − 5 = 4. The key is 4 cm long.

items.q: The ribbon does not start at 0. How many centimetres long is it?
items.e: The ribbon starts at 4, not at 0. Subtract: 15 − 4 = 11. So it is 11 cm long. 15 is where it ends, not how long it is.

items.q: Look at the crayon and the key. Which is true?
items.e: The crayon goes from 0 to 5: 5 cm. The key goes from 3 to 8: 8 − 3 = 5 cm. They are the same length. The key ends at a bigger number, but it also starts later.

items.q: Liam starts a line at 4. He draws it 6 cm long. Where does the line end?
items.e: Start at 4 and count 6 spaces: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. Or add: 4 + 6 = 10. The line ends at 10.

items.q: Mei starts a line at 2. She wants it to be 7 cm long. Where should she stop?
items.e: Start at 2 and count 7 spaces: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Or add: 2 + 7 = 9. Stop at 9. If you stop at 7, the line is only 5 cm long.

items.q: How much longer is the pencil than the crayon?
items.e: Both start at 0. The pencil ends at 12 and the crayon ends at 7. 12 − 7 = 5. The pencil is 5 cm longer.

items.q: How much longer is the straw than the eraser?
items.e: Both start at 0. The straw ends at 10 and the eraser ends at 3. 10 − 3 = 7. The straw is 7 cm longer.

items.q: How much longer is the ribbon than the key?
items.e: Both start at 0. The ribbon ends at 15 and the key ends at 6. 15 − 6 = 9. The ribbon is 9 cm longer.

items.q: How much longer is the marker than the caterpillar?
items.e: Both start at 0. The marker ends at 11 and the caterpillar ends at 5. 11 − 5 = 6. The marker is 6 cm longer.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: The straw goes from 0 to 7: 7 cm. The pencil goes from 5 to 11: 11 − 5 = 6 cm. The straw is longer, even though the pencil ends at a bigger number.

items.q: Which length is the longest?
items.e: 1 m is 100 cm. 100 cm is more than 90, 60 or 45 cm, so 1 m is the longest.

items.q: After the rain, Hana found two worms. One is 12 cm long. The other is 7 cm long. How much longer is the long worm?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 12 − 7 = 5 cm. Or count on from 7 to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. Do not add: 12 + 7 = 19 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Olivia’s paper airplane flew 9 m. Chloe’s flew 6 m. How much farther did Olivia’s airplane fly?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 9 − 6 = 3 m. Or count on from 6 to 9: 7, 8, 9. Do not add: 9 + 6 = 15 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Wei’s pencil was 17 cm long. After a month of school, it is 9 cm long. How much shorter is it now?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 17 − 9 = 8 cm. Do not add: 17 + 9 = 26 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Emma found two cedar sticks. One is 34 cm long. The other is 18 cm long. How much longer is the long stick?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 34 − 18 = 16 cm. Check by adding: 18 + 16 = 34. Do not add: 34 + 18 = 52 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: In Stanley Park, Kai saw a banana slug 18 cm long and a garden slug 7 cm long. How much longer is the banana slug?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 18 − 7 = 11 cm. Do not add: 18 + 7 = 25 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: A bean plant was 14 cm tall. Now it is 31 cm tall. How many centimetres did it grow?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 31 − 14 = 17 cm. Check by adding: 14 + 17 = 31. Do not add: 31 + 14 = 45 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Noah has a ribbon 50 cm long. He cuts off 18 cm for a card. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 50 − 18 = 32 cm. Check by adding: 18 + 32 = 50. Do not add: 50 + 18 = 68 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: In gym class, Arjun jumped 96 cm. Owen jumped 88 cm. How much farther did Arjun jump?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 96 − 88 = 8 cm. Check by adding: 88 + 8 = 96. Do not add: 96 + 88 = 184 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: A sunflower is 92 cm tall. A tomato plant is 58 cm tall. How much taller is the sunflower?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 92 − 58 = 34 cm. Check by adding: 58 + 34 = 92. Do not add: 92 + 58 = 150 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: The Terry Fox Run loop at school is 100 m long. Leah has run 65 m. How many more metres must she run?
items.e: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 100 − 65 = 35 m. Check by adding: 65 + 35 = 100. Do not add: 100 + 65 = 165 is the total, not the difference.

items.q: Harjot’s sandcastle at White Rock beach is 70 cm tall. He wants it to be 1 m tall. How many more centimetres must he build?
items.e: 1 m is 100 cm. 100 − 70 = 30 cm. Count on by 10s from 70: 80, 90, 100. That is 3 tens, or 30.

items.q: Zara makes a paper chain for the classroom door. One part is 45 cm long. Another part is 38 cm long. She joins them. How long is the chain now?
items.e: Joining makes it longer, so add: 45 + 38 = 83 cm. 5 + 8 = 13, so regroup 10 ones as 1 ten.

items.q: Sofia’s little cedar tree was 85 cm tall. This year it grew 12 cm. How tall is it now?
items.e: The tree got taller, so add: 85 + 12 = 97 cm.

items.q: The pool at the community centre is 25 m long. Ava swims to the end and back. How far does she swim?
items.e: To the end is 25 m. Back is 25 m more. 25 + 25 = 50 m.
